title: Baikonur Cosmodrome

place.label: Baikonur Cosmodrome, Kazakhstan
place.basis: One Wikidata (CC0) coordinate for the whole site; a spaceport covers many square kilometres

facts.text: The Soviet Union launched Sputnik, the first artificial satellite, from the Baikonur Cosmodrome in Kazakhstan on 4 October 1957.
NASA describes Sputnik as about the size of a beach ball, roughly 23 inches across and under 190 pounds, circling Earth in about 98 minutes.
ESA says construction of the site began in 1955 and that Sputnik 1 reached orbit on a modified intercontinental ballistic rocket.
ESA says Yuri Gagarin's 12 April 1961 flight, the first crewed orbit of Earth, left from Launch Pad 1.
ESA says the Soviet name Baikonur came from a small mining town about 370 km from the real launch complex, which lies near Tyuratam; the nearby city was renamed Baikonur in 1998.

claims.text: Sputnik 1 was launched from Baikonur on 4 October 1957.

tiers.everyday: Baikonur Cosmodrome in Kazakhstan is where the Soviet Union launched Sputnik, the first artificial satellite, on 4 October 1957. ESA says Yuri Gagarin's first human spaceflight left from here too.
tiers.student: NASA says Sputnik was launched from the Baikonur Cosmodrome on 4 October 1957. ESA says construction began in 1955 and that Yuri Gagarin's 12 April 1961 flight left from Launch Pad 1. The name came from a mining town about 370 km away, used to hide the real site.
